newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's peso closes higher at 1,047.50.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's peso closes higher at 1,047.50.

text.p: Colombia's peso gained 2.5 pesos Tuesday to close at 1,047.50 per dollar after a wave of speculative trading by banks, interbank dealers said.
"Dollars were in short supply early on as traders moved to cover their forward positions," one trader in Medellin said in a telephone interview.
"But that was quickly resolved as coffee and oil exporters fed small amounts back into the market and as financial institutions traded in dollars bought over the last few days," he said.
Dealers reported 387 trades for a total of $156 million.
The peso hit an intraday low of 1,053.7 per dollar around midday but rallied to a high of 1,047.10 before the close. The average exchange rate was 1,052.03 pesos per dollar.

"In previous days there has been heavy demand by banks, which wanted to protect themselves from potential risks created by the announcement of the vice president's resignation, and today they began selling and profit-taking," another trader in Bogota said.
He said the market was fluctuating because of an uncertain political and economic outlook, which created a climate that encourages speculation.

"Given the current levels of volatility, institutions are using every opportunity to take profits. Many are selling and buying in the same day because they look on any profit as a good thing right now," he added.
The trader said there were indications the dollar would pick up slightly in coming days to close the week at about 1,051 or 1,052 pesos.
